questions.question_english: 86. What is the minimum percentage of disability required for an individual to qualify for pension benefits?
questions.explanation_english: Under the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme, a component of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), applicants must demonstrate a minimum disability level of eighty percent to be eligible for pension benefits. This scheme is designed to provide social security pensions to severely disabled individuals who do not have a regular source of income, ensuring that they receive financial support. Additionally, beneficiaries must belong to households classified as below the poverty line and fall within the age range of eighteen to seventy-nine years.
